mission_03: Propensity score matching is one of the most widely used methods for causal inference from observational data. The propensity score e(X) = P(T=1|X) is the probability of receiving treatment given observed covariates. Rosenbaum and Rubin (1983) proved that conditioning on the propensity score is sufficient to remove all confounding bias due to observed covariates. In this mission, you will estimate propensity scores using logistic regression, perform nearest-neighbor matching to pair treated units with similar control units, calculate the Average Treatment Effect on the Treated (ATT), and assess covariate balance using standardized mean differences. This method creates a pseudo-randomized experiment from observational data by ensuring treated and control groups are comparable on observed characteristics.
